extra.message: User-controlled `username` and `password` from request.form are interpolated directly into a SQL query string via an f-string, then executed with c.execute(query). An attacker can submit a username like `' OR '1'='1' --` to bypass authentication or extract data via UNION-based injection.

The /dashboard route performs no server-side authentication check. It only reads a client-supplied `session` cookie (defaulting to 'guest' if absent) and renders content based on it. Since the cookie is never signed or validated (see the set_cookie call in login()), any user can access this route and impersonate any account simply by setting their own cookie value.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The session cookie is set to the raw, unsigned username (`response.set_cookie("session", username)`) with no HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes and no server-side session token/signature. Any client can forge this cookie to impersonate any user (e.g., set cookie `session=admin`), and because HttpOnly is not set, it is also readable/stealable via any XSS on the site.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message:
The `session` cookie value (fully attacker-controlled, see insecure-session-cookie finding) is interpolated directly into an HTML response via an f-string without escaping: f"

Welcome, {user}!

...". An attacker can set a cookie such as `session=` to achieve stored/reflected XSS against any victim who loads this cookie value.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message:
The `q` query parameter from request.args is reflected directly into the HTML response via an f-string without escaping: f"

Search Results for {query}

". A request like /search?q= executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Admin credentials are hardcoded as module-level constants: USERNAME = "admin", PASSWORD = "password123". Hardcoded credentials in source code can be extracted by anyone with code/repo access and are difficult to rotate.

The `users` table stores passwords as plain TEXT and the seed row inserts the plaintext password 'password1' directly (INSERT INTO users (username, password) VALUES ('user1', 'password1')). Passwords are never hashed anywhere in the codebase (login() also compares plaintext at line 33), so a database compromise exposes all user credentials directly.

The /login POST endpoint (and its corresponding form in templates/index.html) has no CSRF token or any anti-CSRF mechanism (e.g., Flask-WTF/CSRFProtect). Combined with the predictable, unsigned session cookie, an attacker can craft a cross-site auto-submitting form to force login state changes for a victim.
